newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Bulgaria may start negotiations for rescheduling of 679 million Ecus of debts to the two banks of the former communist trading bloc Comecon, the International Bank for Economic Cooperation and the International Investment Bank, once the banks agree the conditions for repayment of their debts to creditors, finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said.

-- Parliament's budget and economy committees will discuss this week draft amendments to the Bulgarian National Bank Act and the Banking and Lending Act related to the planned introduction of a currency board.

-- The most likely candidates to head the currency board are Chavdar Kanchev, now chief executive director of Bulgaria's biggest bank Bulbank, and Haralambi Anchev, justice minister in the current interim cabinet.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank plenary council decided that international auditors Deloitte & Touche would carry out the bank's audit for last year. Deloitte & Touche performed the BNB audit for 1995.
-- Consumer prices fell 0.7 percent month on month in April, the first fall since 1990 when Bulgaria launched market reforms and the National Statistics Institute started measuring inflation.

-- Private Elitbank shareholders decided to raise capital nine-fold to 36 billion levs through a new share issue. A potential investor that might be willing to gain control over the bank should buy voting shares worth more than nine billion levs ($6 million), the shareholders decided.

-- A Swiss financial institution bought a nine percent stake in Bulgaria's International Bank for Trade and Development. The bank's registered capital amounts to 13 billion levs of which 3.26 billion levs have been paid in.

-- The Paris Club of government creditors invited Bulgarian officials for talks on rescheduling Bulgaria's debt in a reply to a letter by interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski, Sofianski said in an interview.
